# mcp-proof

> mcp-proof proves that an MCP server really starts in real clients. It runs each client it finds in a throwaway home, makes it start your server, watches the MCP conversation and writes dated, labelled evidence (verified, started, failed, not-installed) as a README table, compat.json and badges. It never installs a client or touches real client settings, and its log holds method names only. MIT licence, by Voyageur Works.

Run it (Node.js 22 or newer): `npx -y @voyageurworks/mcp-proof run -- npx -y your-mcp-server`
In GitHub Actions: `uses: voyageurworks/mcp-proof@v0` with `server:` and `out:`.
